examples.ko: 이 건물은 좌우가 대칭적 구조로 되어 있어요.
examples.en: This building has a symmetrical structure, left and right.

examples.ko: 나비 날개는 대칭적인 무늬를 가지고 있어요.
examples.en: A butterfly's wings have a symmetrical pattern.

examples.ko: 종이를 반으로 대칭적으로 접으면 양쪽이 딱 맞아요.
examples.en: If you fold the paper symmetrically in half, both sides match exactly.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 대칭적이면 더 균형 잡혀 보인다고 해요.
examples.en: They say a symmetrical face looks more balanced.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계는 대칭적이지 않아서 갈등이 많아요.
examples.en: The relationship between the two countries isn't symmetrical, so there is a lot of conflict.

examples.ko: 정원을 대칭적 형태로 꾸미니까 깔끔해 보여요.
examples.en: Decorating the garden in a symmetrical shape makes it look neat.

explain: '대칭'은 명사이고 '대칭적'은 '대칭적인 모양', '대칭적으로'처럼 꾸며 주는 말로 써요. '대칭적 구조'처럼 바로 명사 앞에 붙이기도 해요. 반대는 '비대칭적'이고, 수학·디자인뿐 아니라 두 나라나 두 사람의 관계를 말할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: Snowflakes have a symmetrical shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-인'을 붙여 명사를 꾸미는 활용이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-인' to modify a noun.

phrases.en: I placed the flowers symmetrically and it looks nice.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸미는 부사형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form that modifies a verb.

phrases.en: This bag has an asymmetrical design.
phrases.nuance_ko: '대칭적'의 반대말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 대칭적.

explain_en: '대칭' is the noun, and '대칭적' modifies things, as in '대칭적인 모양' or '대칭적으로'. It can also sit directly before a noun, as in '대칭적 구조'. The opposite is '비대칭적', and it is used for math and design as well as for relationships between countries or people.

examples.en: The baby's face is slightly round, so it's really cute.
This stone is roundish in shape and smooth.
Roundish glasses suit your face well.
I roll the dough so that the bread comes out roundish.
It's a night when the moon looks nearly round.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 제 얼굴이 더 동그스름했어요.
examples.en: My face was rounder when I was little.

explain: '동그랗다'가 또렷한 원 모양이라면, '동그스름하다'는 '조금 동그란 듯하다'는 느낌이에요. 얼굴, 돌, 안경테처럼 완전한 원은 아니지만 부드럽게 둥근 모양에 많이 써요. '둥그스름하다'는 같은 모양을 조금 더 큰 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.

phrases.example: 그 아이는 동그스름한 얼굴이 참 귀여워요.
phrases.en: That child has a lovely softly round face.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사를 꾸밀 때 '-ㄴ' 형태로 바꿔서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Change to the '-ㄴ' form to describe a noun.

phrases.en: This plate is slightly round in shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체로 모양을 설명할 때 쓰는 기본형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic polite form for describing a shape.

phrases.en: The top of the hat is roundish.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하고 조금 더 큰 둥근 모양을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar meaning, used for a somewhat bigger round shape.

explain_en: While '동그랗다' means a clear circle, '동그스름하다' feels like 'somewhat round'. It suits softly rounded shapes that are not perfect circles, such as faces, stones or glasses frames. '둥그스름하다' describes the same kind of shape but with a slightly bigger feel.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 점수가 동률이라서 연장전에 들어갔어요.
examples.en: The two teams' scores were tied, so it went into extra time.
The voting result came out as a tie.
When grades are tied, we decide by drawing lots.
Three people ended up tied for first place.
In the last game they broke the tie and won the title.

examples.ko: 동률인 팀끼리 한 번 더 겨뤄요.
examples.en: The teams that are tied play each other once more.

explain: '무승부'는 경기에서 비긴 결과를 말하고, '동률'은 점수, 표, 순위 같은 숫자가 똑같다는 점에 초점이 있어요. '동률 1위', '동률을 이루다'처럼 순위와 함께 많이 써요.

phrases.en: Two students tied for first place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 순위가 같을 때 숫자 앞에 붙이는 대표적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A typical pairing placed before a rank number when it is shared.

phrases.en: The two candidates tied in the votes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자가 똑같아졌다는 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to state the result that the numbers came out equal.

phrases.example: 마지막 골 덕분에 점수가 동률이 됐어요.
phrases.en: The last goal made the score a tie.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 달랐다가 같아진 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a change from being different to being equal.

explain_en: Formal — equal numbers, scores, or rates between two sides. '무승부' is the result of a game ending in a draw, while '동률' focuses on numbers such as scores, votes or rankings being equal. It is often used with rankings, as in '동률 1위' or '동률을 이루다'.

t90.ax: The voting result came out as a tie.

en: to be sparse; to be thin; to be scattered

examples.en: My hair has thinned, so my front hair is sparse.

examples.ko: 숲의 나무가 듬성듬성해서 햇빛이 잘 들어와요.
examples.en: The trees in the forest are sparse, so sunlight comes in well.
My eyebrows are on the sparse side, so I draw them in every day.
The grass is patchy, so I'll have to sow more seed.
It's winter, so the leaves on the street trees have become sparse.
The audience was thin, but the performance was wonderful.

explain: 머리숱·눈썹·나무·관객처럼 있어야 할 것이 드문드문할 때 써요. 부사 '듬성듬성'과 뜻이 같고, 서술할 때는 '-해요', 꾸밀 때는 '-한'으로 써요. 반대는 '빽빽하다', '촘촘하다'예요.

phrases.en: As I got older, my hair became thin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-해지다'를 붙여 점점 드물어지는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-해지다' expresses a gradual change toward becoming sparse.

phrases.en: I fill in my sparse eyebrows with a pencil.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-한'을 붙여 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The '-한' form modifies the noun that follows.

phrases.example: 이 숲은 나무가 듬성듬성하지 않고 아주 울창해요.
phrases.en: The trees in this forest aren't sparse; it's very dense.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 '빽빽하다'는 뜻을 부드럽게 나타낼 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form softly conveys that something is dense.

explain_en: Use it when things that should be there, like hair, eyebrows, trees or an audience, are thin and scattered. It means the same as the adverb '듬성듬성', used as '-해요' in predicates and '-한' before nouns. Its opposites are '빽빽하다' and '촘촘하다'.

en: to be the same in name and reality

examples.en: He is truly the best singer in our country, in name and reality.

examples.ko: 이 도시는 명실상부하게 문화의 중심이 되었어요.
examples.en: This city has become the cultural center in both name and reality.

examples.ko: 이 학교는 명실상부 우리나라 최고의 대학이에요.
examples.en: This school is truly the best university in our country, in name and in fact.

examples.ko: 그가 명실상부하다는 평가를 받는 이유가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a reason he is regarded as truly deserving of the title.

examples.ko: 명실상부하려면 이름뿐 아니라 실력도 있어야 해요.
examples.en: To live up to the name, you need real skill, not just the name.

examples.ko: 작은 가게였는데 이제는 명실상부한 맛집이 됐어요.
examples.en: It was a small shop, but now it's a truly famous restaurant.

explain: 소문이나 이름과 실제가 서로 맞을 때 쓰는 칭찬이에요. 주로 '명실상부한 + 명사'(최고, 1위, 강팀)로 말해요. 일상 대화에서는 '이름값을 하다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: This team is the undisputed number one.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명실상부한 + 명사' 형태로 이름과 실력이 맞는 최고를 칭찬할 때 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pattern: 명실상부한 + noun, praising someone whose title matches their reality.

phrases.example: 그 도시는 명실상부하게 예술의 중심지가 되었어요.
phrases.en: That city truly became the center of the arts.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사 앞에서 '이름뿐 아니라 실제로도'라는 뜻을 더해 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a verb, it adds the sense of 'in name and in fact'.

phrases.example: 그 식당은 유명한 만큼 이름값을 해요.
phrases.en: That restaurant lives up to its famous name.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명실상부하다'와 비슷한 뜻인데 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual, conversational way to express a similar idea.
phrases.en_equiv: to live up to one's name

explain_en: It is a compliment used when reputation or title and reality match. It is mostly used as '명실상부한 + noun', such as 최고, 1위 or 강팀. In daily talk people also say '이름값을 하다'.

en: to be powerless; to be helpless

examples.ko: 큰 사고 앞에서 저는 너무 무력했어요.
examples.en: In the face of the big accident, I was completely powerless.

examples.ko: 아픈 친구를 보면서 아무것도 못 해 무력하게 느꼈어요.
examples.en: Watching my sick friend, I felt helpless because I could do nothing.

examples.ko: 그는 무력한 표정으로 한참을 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat for a long time with a helpless look.
Since things keep failing, I feel more and more powerless.

examples.ko: 혼자서는 무력하지만 함께하면 달라질 수 있어요.
examples.en: Alone we are powerless, but together things can change.

examples.ko: 너무 무력해서 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: I felt so helpless that I couldn't say anything.

explain: '무력하다'는 상황 앞에서 내가 할 수 있는 힘이나 방법이 없다는 느낌이에요. 의욕이 없어서 힘이 빠진 '무기력하다'와 달라요. 무력한 것은 힘이 없는 쪽이고, 무기력한 것은 하고 싶은 마음이 없는 쪽이에요.

phrases.example: 아무것도 못 하고 무력하게 서 있었어요.
phrases.en: I stood there helplessly, unable to do anything.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무력하게' 형태로 동작을 꾸며요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form 무력하게 modifies an action.

phrases.en: As failures repeated, I gradually became powerless.
phrases.nuance_ko: 점점 힘이 없다고 느끼게 되는 변화를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes the change of gradually feeling powerless.

phrases.en: That day I felt a great sense of powerlessness.
phrases.nuance_ko: 힘이 없다는 느낌을 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun for the feeling of having no power.

explain_en: Feeling no strength to act, often an emotional state (무력해지다) 무력하다 is the feeling that you have no power or way to act in a situation. It differs from 무기력하다, which means lacking the will or energy to do anything. 무력하다 is about having no ability, and 무기력하다 is about having no drive.

t90.ax: He sat for a long time with a helpless look.

en: to be common; to be mediocre

examples.en: That child has an extraordinary look in the eyes.

examples.ko: 범상한 사람이라면 그런 결정을 못 했을 거예요.
examples.en: An ordinary person couldn't have made that decision.
From the first impression, he was no ordinary person.

examples.ko: 이 그림은 범상해 보여도 사실 아주 유명해요.
examples.en: This painting looks ordinary, but it is actually very famous.
The atmosphere felt unusual, so I was careful.

examples.ko: 그는 이 일을 범상하게 넘기지 않았어요.
examples.en: He did not let this matter pass as something ordinary.

explain: 대부분 '범상치 않다/범상하지 않다'로 써서 '보통이 아니다, 뭔가 특별하다'는 놀람이나 칭찬을 나타내요. '범상하다'만 쓰는 경우는 글에서 가끔 보여요. 일상에서는 '평범하다'를 써요.

phrases.example: 그 사람에게서 범상치 않은 분위기가 느껴져요.
phrases.en: I sense an extraordinary air about that person.
phrases.nuance_ko: '범상하다'는 거의 '범상하지 않다/범상치 않다' 형태로 써서 '보통이 아니다'라는 뜻을 나타내요.
phrases.nuance_en: 범상하다 is almost always used as 범상하지 않다/범상치 않다, meaning 'not ordinary'.

phrases.example: 범상한 사람은 이런 일을 하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: An ordinary person would find it hard to do this.
phrases.nuance_ko: 글에서 '평범한 사람'을 조금 딱딱하게 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A somewhat formal, written way to say an ordinary person.

phrases.en: That person looks ordinary on the outside.
phrases.nuance_ko: '범상하다'와 같은 뜻으로 일상에서 훨씬 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 범상하다 but far more common in daily speech.

explain_en: It is mostly used in the negative, '범상치 않다/범상하지 않다', to express that someone or something is out of the ordinary, with surprise or praise. The plain affirmative '범상하다' shows up only occasionally in writing. In daily speech, '평범하다' is how you say ordinary.

t90.ax: The atmosphere felt unusual, so I was careful.

en: to be decent; to be presentable; to be respectable

examples.ko: 변변한 옷 한 벌 없이 겨울을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I spent the winter without even one decent coat.
It's a humble gift, but please accept it.

examples.ko: 저는 변변하지 못해서 부모님께 늘 죄송해요.
examples.en: I'm not much to be proud of, so I always feel sorry to my parents.
It's a modest meal, but please eat plenty.

examples.ko: 그 집 아들은 변변해서 어디 가도 걱정 없어요.
examples.en: Their son is decent, so there's no worry wherever he goes.
I'm sorry I couldn't prepare a proper meal for you.

explain: 대부분 '변변하지 않다/못하다', '변변치 않다', '변변찮다'처럼 부정으로 써요. '변변치 않은 선물이지만'은 선물을 줄 때 자신을 낮추는 인사말이에요. '제대로 된'이라는 뜻으로 바꿔 말할 수 있어요.

phrases.en: It's not much of a meal, but please eat a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '변변하지 않다'의 줄임말이에요. 손님에게 음식을 내며 자신을 낮출 때 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened form of 변변하지 않다. Often used humbly when offering food to guests.

phrases.en: I'm worried because I don't have a decent job yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤에 '없다'가 오는 경우가 많고, 제대로 된 직장이 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Usually followed by 없다, meaning there is no proper job.

phrases.en: The house is small and the furniture is meager too.
phrases.nuance_ko: '못하다'와 함께 써서 가진 것이 제대로 갖춰지지 못했다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 못하다 to say that what one has is not properly adequate.

explain_en: Mostly negative: not even decent (변변한 옷이 없다) It is mostly used in the negative: '변변하지 않다/못하다', '변변치 않다', '변변찮다'. '변변치 않은 선물이지만' is a humble phrase used when giving a gift. You can think of it as 'proper' or 'decent' in meaning.

t90.ax: It's a humble gift, but please accept it.

examples.ko: 지역마다 소득이 불균등해서 문제가 되고 있어요.
examples.en: Income is unequal from region to region, which has become a problem.
If resources are divided unevenly, complaints arise.

examples.ko: 교육 기회의 불균등을 줄이는 정책이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need policies that reduce inequality in educational opportunity.
I'm worried about the uneven development of cities and the countryside.

examples.ko: 이 그래프는 인구가 불균등하게 퍼져 있다는 걸 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This graph shows that the population is spread unevenly.

examples.ko: 일을 불균등하게 나누면 팀 분위기가 나빠져요.
examples.en: If you divide the work unevenly, the team atmosphere gets worse.

explain: '불평등'은 대우나 권리가 같지 않을 때 많이 쓰고, '불균등'은 양이나 분포가 고르지 않다는 느낌이 강해요. 보통 '불균등하다', '불균등하게'처럼 활용해서 써요.

phrases.en: Development is uneven across regions.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불균등'을 형용사로 바꿔서 상태를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form of 불균등, used to describe a state.

phrases.en: The budget was spent unevenly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 동사를 꾸미는 부사 형태로, 나눠 쓰는 일에 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form modifying a verb, often used for how things are shared.

phrases.en: The height of the ground is not even.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말로, 딱딱한 '불균등'을 대신해요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday phrase that replaces the formal 불균등.

explain_en: Unevenness between regions or amounts (지역 불균등); more about distribution than fairness. '불평등' is often used when treatment or rights are not the same, while '불균등' leans toward amounts or distribution not being even. It is usually used as '불균등하다' or '불균등하게'.

t90.ax: If resources are divided unevenly, complaints arise.

examples.ko: 이 옷은 한쪽 소매만 길어서 디자인이 비대칭이에요.
examples.en: Only one sleeve of this outfit is long, so the design is asymmetrical.
I was worried because I was told my face is asymmetrical.
The asymmetrical building is a landmark of the city.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 군사력은 비대칭이라서 협상이 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: The two countries' military strength is asymmetrical, so negotiations are not easy.
Asymmetrical hairstyles are popular these days.

examples.ko: 자세가 나쁘면 몸이 비대칭으로 변할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Bad posture can make your body become asymmetrical.

explain: 반대말은 '대칭'이에요. 얼굴, 몸, 디자인처럼 모양뿐 아니라 '정보 비대칭'처럼 힘이나 정보의 차이가 고르지 않을 때도 써요.

phrases.example: 이 건물은 좌우가 대칭이라서 안정돼 보여요.
phrases.en: This building is symmetrical left and right, so it looks stable.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비대칭'의 반대말로, 양쪽이 같은 모양일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 비대칭; used when both sides have the same shape.

phrases.en: Asymmetrical bags are popular these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일부러 양쪽을 다르게 만든 옷이나 물건을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for clothes or items deliberately made different on each side.

phrases.example: 정보 비대칭 때문에 소비자가 손해를 봐요.
phrases.en: Consumers lose out because of information asymmetry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한쪽만 더 많이 알고 있어서 고르지 않은 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes an uneven situation where only one side knows more.

explain_en: The opposite is '대칭'. Besides shapes such as faces, bodies and designs, it is also used for uneven power or information, as in '정보 비대칭'.

examples.ko: 이 영화는 속도감이 있어서 지루하지 않아요.
examples.en: This movie has a fast pace, so it is not boring.

examples.ko: 속도감 있는 음악이라 운동할 때 들어요.
examples.en: It is fast-paced music, so I listen to it when I work out.
I sat in the very front seat to feel the speed.
This game is full of speed, so it is fun.
I was amazed by the sense of speed as the scenery rushed past the window.
The sense of speed is great, but it makes me a little dizzy.

explain: '속도'는 빠르기 자체이고, 속도감은 빠르다고 느껴지는 느낌이에요. 영화, 음악, 게임, 글의 흐름처럼 '속도감 있다/넘치다'로 자주 말해요.

phrases.en: The story moves along at a quick pace.
phrases.nuance_ko: '있게'를 붙여 어떤 일이 빠르게 진행되는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: With '있게', it describes something moving ahead quickly.

phrases.en: You can feel the speed when you ride this car.
phrases.nuance_ko: 실제로 빠르다고 몸이나 눈으로 느낄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you actually feel the speed with your body or eyes.

phrases.example: 이 게임은 속도감이 없어서 조금 심심해요.
phrases.en: This game has no sense of speed, so it's a little boring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 느리고 답답하다고 느낄 때 반대로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite use, when something feels slow and dull.

explain_en: '속도' is speed itself, while 속도감 is the feeling of things moving fast. It is commonly used for movies, music, games and writing, as in '속도감 있다' or '속도감이 넘치다'.

t90.ax: This game is full of speed, so it is fun.

en: to be miraculous; to be incredible

examples.ko: 아이가 혼자 신발을 신다니 참 신통해요.
examples.en: It's amazing that the child puts on shoes alone.
After I took the medicine, my fever went down amazingly well.
This method wasn't all that effective.
There was no clever way, so I just waited.
My grades aren't great, so my parents are worried.

examples.ko: 강아지가 길을 찾아 돌아오다니 정말 신통했어요.
examples.en: It was truly remarkable that the puppy found its way back.

explain: 어린아이나 동물이 기특한 일을 했을 때와 효과가 놀랍게 좋을 때 쓰는데, 비슷한 말로 '대견하다'가 있어요. 부정형 '신통찮다/신통치 않다'는 '별로예요, 시원치 않아요'라는 뜻으로 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: My results on this test aren't very impressive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대만큼 좋지 않다는 뜻으로 일상에서 가장 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means not as good as hoped; the most common everyday use.

phrases.example: 이 약은 감기에 신통한 효과가 있어요.
phrases.en: This medicine has a wonderful effect on colds.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결과가 놀랄 만큼 좋을 때 '효과'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '효과' when the result is surprisingly good.

phrases.en: It's amazing that our puppy understands what I say.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기특한 일을 보고 귀엽게 칭찬하는 구어체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A cute, spoken way to praise something clever.

explain_en: It is used when a child or animal does something admirable, or when something works surprisingly well; '대견하다' is a similar word. The negative form '신통찮다/신통치 않다' is commonly used to mean 'not great' or 'unsatisfying'.

en: to be mottled; to be spotted

examples.en: Maybe I washed it wrong, because the white shirt is blotchy.
I have a cat with a mottled pattern.
The paint was applied unevenly on the wall.
My face got blotchy from sunburn.
It rained, so the road was spotted with wet patches.
Please apply it evenly so it doesn't look blotchy.

explain: 색이 고르지 않고 얼룩이 진 모습이에요. '알록달록'은 여러 고운 색이 섞인 예쁜 모습이라서, 색이 고르지 않아 지저분해 보일 때는 '얼룩덜룩'을 써요.

phrases.en: It's a puppy with a mottled pattern.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-ㄴ'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줘요. 색이 고르지 않은 모양을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form describes the noun after it, meaning an uneven color pattern.

phrases.en: The wall is blotchy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금의 모양을 말하는 해요체예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite present form, describing how it looks now.

phrases.en: My arms got blotchy from sunburn.
phrases.nuance_ko: 색이 고르지 않게 변하는 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes changing into an uneven color.

explain_en: It describes color that is uneven and patchy. '알록달록' means many pretty colors mixed together, so use '얼룩덜룩' when the color is uneven and looks messy.

examples.ko: 외견상 문제가 없어 보여도 안을 확인해야 해요.
examples.en: Even if it looks fine on the outside, you should check the inside.

examples.ko: 이 차는 외견상 새 차와 다를 게 없어요.
examples.en: This car looks no different from a new one.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 외견상 아주 건강해 보였어요.
examples.en: On the surface, he looked very healthy.

examples.ko: 외견상으로는 두 제품이 똑같아서 구별하기 어려워요.
examples.en: The two products look identical, so they are hard to tell apart.

examples.ko: 외견상 차분해 보여도 속은 많이 떨고 있었어요.
examples.en: Although he looked calm on the outside, he was shaking a lot inside.

examples.ko: 외견상 큰 차이는 없지만 성능은 많이 달라요.
examples.en: There's no big difference in looks, but the performance is very different.

explain: '겉으로 보기에'라는 뜻으로 쓰고, 뒤에 '하지만', '그래도'처럼 겉과 속이 다르다는 말이 자주 와요. 일상 대화에서는 '겉보기에'가 더 편하고, '외관상'과도 거의 비슷하게 써요.

phrases.en: Outwardly, there seems to be no problem.
phrases.nuance_ko: '으로는'을 붙이면 겉모습만 보면 그렇다는 뜻이 더 분명해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 'euroneun' makes it clearer that this holds only by appearance.

phrases.en: By its look, this fruit is very fresh.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 같고, 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning, and more casual for daily conversation.

phrases.example: 이 가방은 외관상 비싸 보이지 않아요.
phrases.en: This bag doesn't look expensive by its appearance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 거의 같은 뜻이고, 물건이나 건물에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Almost the same, used more often for objects and buildings.

explain_en: How it seems, may differ from reality (외견상 그 가게는 작아 보이지만 안은 넓어요.) It is used like 'on the surface', and is often followed by a contrast such as '하지만' showing that the outside and inside differ. In daily talk '겉보기에' feels more casual, and it is used almost the same as '외관상'.

t90.ax: On the surface, he looked very healthy.

en: to be bulky; to be brawny

examples.ko: 마을 입구에 우람한 느티나무가 서 있어요.
examples.en: A huge zelkova tree stands at the village entrance.
That player has broad, sturdy shoulders.
The mountain is so massive that you feel overwhelmed looking up at it.
Compared with his burly build, his voice was small.
The building rises up grandly.
Before I knew it, my son had become a strapping young man.

explain: 나무, 산, 건물, 체격이 크고 힘 있고 듬직해 보일 때 써요. 감탄하거나 믿음직하다는 좋은 느낌이에요. '우락부락하다'는 거칠어 보이지만 '우람하다'는 무섭다기보다 당당한 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: A mighty mountain is in front of me.
phrases.nuance_ko: 크고 듬직한 자연이나 건물에 쓰는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The basic form for something big and sturdy in nature or buildings.

phrases.en: That tree looks massive even from far away.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보기에 크고 힘 있다는 느낌을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Says something looks big and strong.

phrases.en: My uncle has a sturdy build.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 몸을 말할 때 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common phrase for a person's body.

explain_en: It is used for trees, mountains, buildings or physiques that look big, strong and dependable, usually with admiration. '우락부락하다' looks rough, while '우람하다' feels imposing rather than scary.
